title: Natural ordinary ring diagram for completed and native coefficients
statement: Fix a prime l, NativeRings l, a finite coefficient index E in PadicAlgCl l, and a Change a from the completed coefficient system of Coefficient E to nativeCoefficients l agreeing with every normalized integralMap [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-compact-support-data], [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-realization-data]. There exists a NativeScalarRingModel l E a: for every scheme T there are isomorphisms from the underlying RingCat-valued completed and native sheaves to the section rings of the pulled condensed integer ring of E and the pulled condensed algebraic closure. They carry a.map to the section-ring map of the composite integer-to-field-to-closure inclusion. For every g:U→V and every site object W, evaluation of both isomorphisms identifies the adjunct of each coefficient inverse-image isomorphism with the condensed precomposition map [lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport]. The exact pointwise naturality and scalar equations are the fields of NativeScalarRingModel. Its module equivalences are constructed by ringModuleEquivalenceOfIso followed by the inverse internal/section equivalence [def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding]; no derived categories or scalar mates occur in this conclusion.

source.place: Formal properties: scalar adjunction mates, composition, and computation of restriction on underlying complexes; coefficient identifications in steps 1–3 of lem-sf-native-proper-scalar-mate-presentation. Also Bhatt–Scholze, Lemma 6.8.2 and Remark 6.8.15.

proof.text: Apply the normalized continuous integral coefficient comparison to the size model Coefficient E. Transport continuous functions through Shrink.algEquiv. The induced finite-dimensional algebra linear equivalence is bicontinuous over Q_l, and uniqueness of the extension of the absolute value identifies the integer subrings. The inverse-limit description of the pulled condensed integers and section reconstruction give the integral ring isomorphism. The finite quotient projection equations normalize it.

Use the locally finite coefficient-ring realization and the internal-to-section equivalence to obtain the closure ring isomorphism in the opposite direction. Its IsMonHom equation preserves multiplication and one; therefore it is a ring-sheaf isomorphism, not merely an additive isomorphism.

Obtain a normalized coefficient presentation using coefficientPresentations_exists. The integral finite-quotient normalization, localization normalization, and normalization on each finite-field leg identify their composite with the integralMap of any CoefficientPresentation. The hypothesis ha therefore gives the scalar equation with the composite of the two actual condensed inclusions.

Take the adjoints of the inverse-image ring maps. The chart naturality and native pull_normalized equations identify both with precomposition of continuous functions. Evaluation on each site object proves integral_natural and closure_natural. This verifies the ring diagram also for identity maps and empty schemes.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_nativeScalarRingModel
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] [N : NativeRings.{u} l]
    (E : Index l (PadicAlgCl l))
    (a : PurCompactSupport.Change (PurCompactSupport.completed l
      (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E)) (nativeCoefficients l))
    (ha : ∀ (T : Scheme.{u})
      (C : CoefficientPresentation l T (Coefficient.{u} l (PadicAlgCl l) E) (embedding l E)),
      a.map T = C.integralMap l T) :
    Nonempty (NativeScalarRingModel l E a)
